summary.name: Dimly
summary.one_liner: Dimly is a macOS menu bar app for controlling brightness, blackout, sleep/wake and profiles per display across mixed external monitor setups.
use_cases: adjust brightness on several external monitors from the menu bar
switch display profiles for color or preview work
keep consistent monitor behavior across docks and offices
control many displays quickly in trading or ops setups
summary.what_it_does: Dimly provides a single menu bar control point for each connected display, letting you adjust brightness, blackout, sleep and wake, rename displays, and copy display IDs. It uses DDC/CI hardware brightness and power controls when a monitor supports them and falls back to a software overlay when it does not. Users can save monitor states as profiles, surface them in Quick Actions, and auto-apply a profile when an external display connects. Global hotkeys can target all external displays or specific ones, with a fixed panic shortcut to restore everything.
notable: Automatic DDC/CI hardware control with overlay fallback for monitors without DDC support
Panic shortcut to restore all displays instantly
No telemetry, no daemons; Sparkle updates with signature verification and notarized builds
Stealth mode hides Dock and menu bar icon
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page; the awesome-mac listing describes it as freeware while also marking it open source on GitHub
Overlay fallback is used when DDC is not supported, so it is a software dimming approach rather than hardware control in those cases
